chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Durays, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

“The legal punishments that belong to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are not pardoned apart from the Imam. As for what is from the rights of people within a legal punishment, there is no harm in it being pardoned apart from the Imam.”

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam as the rightful authority
key_terms.حَقِّ النَّاسِ: the rights or claims of people
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: belonging to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic

ai.seo_question: Who can pardon hudud punishments in cases involving the rights of Allah and the rights of people?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between two kinds of claims within legal punishments: the rights of Allah and the rights of people. It states that hudud belonging to Allah cannot be remitted by anyone short of the Imam, while a personal claim belonging to people may be waived without the Imam.
